summary: Planned the answered 'Case Escalation Email Alert to Account Owner' requirement at scale feature (O=2 named objects, Case and Account, is the signal that promoted it past ask) into exactly one milestone (M1) and one step (M1-S01, type automation, agent metadata-builder, human_gate false). The step builds one after-save record-triggered Flow on Case (Update, fires on every transition to IsEscalated=true) that reads the related Account's Owner and sends an email with the Case Number and Subject via a Flow Send Email action, with an explicit skip-and-log path for no-Account and a Support-Manager fallback for a Queue-owned Account, and a fault path per templates/flow/FaultPath_Template.md. Recorded one fit_gap row (Low-Code, effort M, fit) and two decisions, both resolved via decision-tree branches with adr_required false: D1 (automation-selection.md Q4, Flow over the native Escalation Rule engine's fixed-recipient notify actions or Apex) and D2 (flow-pattern-selector.md Q5, After-Save firing inline over Before-Save or a Scheduled Path). No assumptions were needed -- all 4 blocking clarifications were answered directly (none deferred) and all 15 informational rows carry the clarifier's pre-filled defaults as answers, not open deferrals. Wrote the plan body via set-plan, validated (0 warnings on the first pass), and rendered PLAN.md/CLARIFICATIONS.md. Status is now planned; gate 'plan' is pending.
confidence_rationale: Every blocking clarification was answered (not deferred); the step's agent (metadata-builder: class runtime, status beta, requires_org false) is eligible in this design-only build; both cited skills and both their checkers and both cited templates resolve on disk; both decisions cite a decision-tree branch (not a source_reference fallback) with a verbatim branch_quote; the step carries four acceptance tests (two checkers, xml, manifest) whose runners all exist; validate exits 0 with 0 steps blocked and 0 warnings -- every clause of the agent's own HIGH bar is met.

process_observations.observation: Both technology decisions (Flow over the native Escalation Rule engine; After-Save over Before-Save) resolved cleanly to a decision-tree branch on the first read, with no need to fall back to a source_reference/adr_required:true pair -- unlike the opp-amount-lock precedent build, where neither of its two decisions was tree-covered.

Reading skills/admin/escalation-rules/SKILL.md's Core Concepts table before writing D1 caught a real design trap: the native Escalation Rule engine's notifyTo/notifyEmail/notifyCaseOwner actions target a fixed user, role, or the case owner, never a dynamically-resolved 'Owner of the related Account' -- so the native engine cannot satisfy this requirement even in an org that already has Escalation Rules configured. Confirming this before committing to Flow avoided a plan that looked plausible ('use the existing escalation mechanism') but could not have been built.

The sizing-rule promotion from 'ask' to 'feature' rests entirely on O=2 (Case and Account both named in the one-sentence requirement) even though the automation itself is exactly as small as the worked 'ask'-tier validation-rule example in standards/build-orchestration.md Section 3.1 (one Flow, one milestone, one step). A reader skimming only the automation complexity, not the object count, would reasonably expect scale:ask here; the O-signal promotion is correct per the letter of the sizing table but produces more ceremony (a feature-tier clarification round, a milestone-only-not-RUN.md documentation path) than the build's actual size seems to warrant.

Whether admin/escalation-rules, admin/case-management-setup, and admin/assignment-rules should have been kept in the clarifier's harvested skill set (they surfaced in the capability searches and each carries a Questions-to-Ask table) is a judgment call this run made by scoping: the requirement reacts to an existing escalation state rather than asking to build or change the escalation/routing mechanism itself, so their design-the-mechanism questions were treated as out of scope rather than harvested. A different, more literal reading of Step 3's 'keep every skill that has one' would have harvested all three, which -- given each contributes at least one more named object or supporting metadata type -- would plausibly have re-tiered this build to 'project'.
The plan is written, validated (0 warnings) and rendered; the next stage in the loop is the adversarial three-lens verification before the human plan gate.
